show.name: Gŵyl ABERTEIFI LIVE 2026
show.description:
30th + 31st October 2026 

Following the announcement that Other Voices Cardigan is taking a fallow year in 2026, we promised we wouldn’t let October pass without a celebration of incredible live music in our town. 

See the full schedule at aberteifilive.co.uk 

The ABERTEIFI LIVE collective, a partnership formed of local music champions: Mwldan, Fflach, Small World Theatre, The Cellar and GRAIN, is thrilled to share the first wave of artists for our brand-new grassroots music weekend on 30–31 October 2026. We have curated a line-up designed to capture that intimate, unmistakable festival magic that transforms Aberteifi every autumn, spanning folk, grime, indie, soul and electronica and much, much more… 

Aloka/ Cerys Hafana/ Dani Larkin/ EtrA/ Filmore!/ Kizzy Crawford/ Lemoncello/ Mace The Great/ Mared/ MORN/ Muireann Ní Shé/ SLATE/ Tai Haf Heb Drigolyn/ Tokomololo/ Tessio 

 + DJ Sets from MR A/ ANDY SONIC/ ELISHEA/ GOOD NATURE PARTY/ YANN DE GALLES + AWEN 

Talks with speakers: Anna Nicoll AS/MS/ Cerys Hafana/ Dilwyn Davies/ Filmore!/ Gethin Scourfield/ Hannah Firth/ Lemoncello/ Mared / Nico Dafydd / Sarah James 


Over the course of two days, more than 40 live gigs will take over five of Cardigan’s most beloved independent venues: Mwldan, Small World Theatre, Bethania, GRAIN and The Cellar. 

You can find out more about the artists and listen to the festival playlist over at the Aberteifi Live website aberteifilive.co.uk 

Because this event is stepping into a fallow year, it is operating entirely without public subsidy. It is funded 100% by ticket sales and the incredible generosity of our local business sponsors. We have intentionally kept ticket prices to an absolute minimum (£55 for adults, and just £15 for Under 18s) to ensure the whole community can join the party. Because of the intimate nature of the event, capacity is limited. The best way to show your support for Cardigan’s autumn festival weekend is to gather your gig buddies, book your tickets early and help us spread the word. Join us to make this an unmissable weekend of live music and magic! 


Ticket Info: 

Weekend Tickets: £55 (a limited number of Under 18s tickets are available for £15) 


Gŵyl ABERTEIFI LIVE is grateful to Culture Ireland for their support of this event.

show.name: 7Steps: The Music of Miles Davis
show.description:
Trumpeter Tomos Williams brings his band of brilliant musicians to Mwldan for the first time to play the music of jazz legend Miles Davis. 


7Steps perform some of the classics associated with the great trumpeter; So What, All Blues, Milestones but also play some of the less well known songs from Miles' vast catalogue such as Joshua, Masqualero and Teo. 2026 is the centenary year of Miles Davis' birth, and 7Steps will perform the music of one of the towering figures of 20th Century music, with passion and vigour. 


The quintet, includes stellar Welsh jazz musicians Joe Northwood on tenor sax, pianist Dave Jones,Paula Gardiner on bass and the magnificent Mark O'Connor on drums. Tomos Williams is a leading and unique voice on the Welsh jazz scene. Heavily indebted and influenced by Miles' music ,7Steps is a natural project for Tomos to front. Tomos also leads the jazz/folk sextet, Burum, the groundbreaking Indo-Welsh fusion band 'Khamira', (who have played in South Korea, India and Wales) and his Cwmwl Tystion/Witness project. 7Steps have toured Wales in 2018 and 2023, and their concerts paying homage to Miles Davis and his music are always popular. 


Get your tickets early for a night of swinging jazz and burning solos. 


  • 'Williams guides the band, and he stalks the stage half-proud father and half-explorer in a new, dangerous, but familiar land. His horn is beautifully controlled, pulling soloists back to the root of the number, springboarding them off’ 
– Wales Arts Review

show.name: Beatles Complete

Direct from the world famous Cavern Club, Liverpool


Remember the time when music made you feel excited and alive, when every new song grabbed you and wouldn't let go? Well … Beatles Complete are returning to Mwldan for one unforgettable night of pure Beatlemania. 



Based in Liverpool and performing regularly at the world-famous Cavern Club for the last 4 years (over 300 times and counting), Beatles Complete have built a reputation as one of the most exciting and authentic Beatles tribute acts around. In fact, when they started they became the youngest ever Beatles band to secure a residency at the iconic venue where the Fab Four story began. From the raw excitement of She Loves You to the timeless brilliance of Let It Be, this electrifying live show captures the sound, style and spirit of The Beatles at the height of their fame. Expect period-accurate instruments, stunning vocal harmonies, and all the energy and charm that made four lads from Liverpool a worldwide phenomenon. 



This isn’t just a tribute show — it’s a journey back to the music that defined a generation.

This year, we present a new film produced by Gary Evans of Cilgerran. For many in the area, the line was the focus of the local community, gaining the nickname the Cardi Bach. Owen Shiers brings Cynefin to the stage with his band, performing music rooted in the songs, stories and landscape of his native Ceredigion. Drawing on years of research into the vernacular traditions of west Wales, Owen breathes new life into forgotten songs and voices through inventive arrangements and original compositions. 


His acclaimed albums Dilyn Afon and Shimli have established Cynefin as a distinctive voice in contemporary Welsh folk music. Most recently, Shimli was nominated for UK Folk Album of the Year 2025 and named The Guardian’s Folk Album of the Month.

'A Festive Story to Ring the Old Year Out and the New Year In'


It is Christmas 1950 in New York and the actors of WAFR: Playhouse of the Air gather for their annual festive broadcast...


There is a new government, a new hope, a new world, so what bet-ter than a new play? And there is no better story-teller than Charles Dickens - and there is no better man to keep Christmas than he! Trotty Veck is a ticket-porter – a man who fetches and carries packages, letters and deliveries for a small sixpence here and there. He doesn’t have much but he is happy, gentle and lives a simple, obedient life. That life is given its order by the sound of the bells of his local church – breakfast, lunch, dinner all from the sound of the bells. He sometimes even hears them speaking to him… In the run-up to the festive season Trotty falls asleep after a long day’s carrying and delivering. Woken by the church bells, The Chimes, and then summoned up the tower by their mysterious power, he has just one chance to change this world… but will he listen to the bells? The Chimes is a Victorian It’s a Wonderful Life filled with all of the master story-teller’s colourful characters and heart-rending poignancy. Fresh from their hugely popular adaptations of A Christmas Carol and Casablanca, Lighthouse Theatre brings their signature live radio play style to this classic by the most theatrical of authors. 


There will be jingles, carols, music and – of course – bells!…this show is sure to be fast and funny, inventive and entertaining; but most of all a Christmas treat to reinforce the message of this festive time of the year…

show.name: Ranagri
show.description:
Ranagri's Say Hello Tour heralds a bold new era for this award-winning indie folk band, bringing their signature cinematic, prog-infused folk music to venues up and down the UK this Autumn. With five studio albums under their belt, a wealth of international touring experience, and standout appearances at major festivals, Ranagri have built a formidable reputation on the global stage, captivating audiences from across Europe to Australia, Montreal and New Orleans. 


Now, they turn inward, reconnecting with their roots for what promises to be their most evocative and personal tour to date. Steeped in stories of Ranagri - the farmland in rural Ireland from which the band takes its name - their new album explores themes of migration, identity, and the enduring search for the meaning of home. It is a work of depth and resonance, shaped by lived experiences and a profound sense of place. Renowned for their commanding live performances, the band delivers a sound that is both intricate and expansive. Soaring vocals, rich harmonies, and driving rhythmic energy intertwine with masterful instrumentation - flutes, whistles, harp, bodhrán, hammered dulcimer, percussion and guitars - forming a virtuosic and immersive soundscape around lead singer Dónal Rogers. The result is a musical experience that feels at once intimate, powerful, and unmistakably anthemic.

show.name: Simon Yates: My Mountain Life
show.description:
A fascinating and humorous evening, acclaimed by both regular theatre patrons and outdoor enthusiasts alike. 

On the remote Siula Grande in Peru in June 1985, mountaineer Simon Yates found himself in a desperately unenviable position. He was slowly being pulled off the mountain face by his injured partner, Joe Simpson, dangling on the rope 50 metres below. His decision to cut the rope saved both their lives in the epic tale of survival that followed. With the publication of the book ‘Touching The Void’, which later became a film and stage play, both climbers became household names. 

It was an experience that could have put many off the sport of mountaineering - but not Simon. Over 35 years later, he is still a very active exploratory climber and guide, making several expeditions to the mountains each year. From the Arctic to the Antarctic, Alaska to Central Asia, there is hardly a significant range that he has not visited. 

Come along and witness Simon’s tireless journey from that mountain in Peru to some of the remotest on the planet and share with him the drama, excitement and beauty of modern, lightweight alpinism. Told with wit, dry humour and lavishly illustrated with images and film footage collected on his great climbs.

show.name: The Budapest Café Orchestra

Refreshingly unconventional and snappily attired boutique orchestra. Budapest Café Orchestra bring you gypsy and folk-flavoured music in their own fresh and surprising way. With 14 albums to their name the Budapest Café Orchestra was established in 2009 by British composer and violinist, Christian Garrick, and led by him have won legions of fans with their magical and infectious performances. A small but impeccably formed ensemble of just four players, the BCO combines violin, guitar, accordion, double bass, saz & balalaika to dazzling effect, creating an awesome aural alchemy normally only characteristic of far larger ensembles. 


Evoking vivid images of Tzigane fiddle maestros, Budapest café life and gypsy campfires - plus a few surprises along the way - hugely entertaining, immense skill and profound musicianship, a show by the BCO is enough to make you want to book that holiday down the Danube!
